Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report.

In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that the applicant used to promise marriage with the victim and as such,
took her on 27.07.2019.
On going with her, she deciphered that the applicant was a Muslim by religion.
Allegations were leveled against the family members that they used to get beef cooked from her.
The age of the victim as per the medical report is 18 years.

3. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

4. Considering the statements on record, it appears that the allegations were leveled on the ground that there was false pretext of marriage.
The victim knew the applicant for almost five months.
The victim also stayed in the house of the applicant.
The applicant is in custody since 05.11.2019 and has no criminal antecedents, and the trial has not even started.

As such, on the basis of the statement as well as on prima-facie, violation of the applicant's right of speedy trial under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Arif @ Khurshid Ahmad be released on bail in FIR No.419 of 2019 under Section 363, 366, 376 IPC & Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, P.S. Kotwali Akbarpur, District Ambedkar Nagar on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
